children: Apotex Health increased its full-year outlook after new drug launches and higher sales drove fiscal second-quarter earnings higher.
The Canadian pharmaceutical company said Thursday that it now expects revenue to grow between 9% and 10% in fiscal 2027, up from a previous expectation of between 7% and 8%.
It also expects the adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization margin to be 31%, compared with 30%.

Apotex, a Canadian pharmaceutical company specializing in generic, biosimilar, and branded specialty medications, said the rosier outlook follows a strong operational performance in the first half, driven by the launches of new drugs and accelerating revenue growth.

The revision comes alongside the company's fiscal second-quarter results, where Apotex reported a rise in net income to 100.8 million Canadian dollars ($70.7 million) for the three months ended Sept. 30, up from C$82.9 million in the comparable quarter a year prior.
On a per-share basis, earnings fell to C$0.41 a share from C$0.43 a share due to a higher share count following Apotex's recent initial public offering.
Adjusted earnings, which exclude revenue from its U.S. generic version of the blood cancer drug Revlimid, came to C$0.57 a share. According to FactSet, analysts were expecting C$0.37 a share.
Revenue rose 1.1% to C$852.9 million. When stripping out prior-year Revlimid sales, sales climbed 4.9%, topping consensus expectations for C$828.3 million.
Apotex benefited from a surge in Canadian sales, which rose nearly 15%, as well as branded and biosimilar expansion, which saw an 18% rise. Conventional generics rose 11%.
